ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT statute: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended. Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31 and Part XII.1. UBO statutes: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (register of Individuals with Significant Control), as amended by S.C. 2023, c. 26 authorizing the Canadian public beneficial ownership registry, with filing obligations effective 22 January 2024; Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, s. 140.1 requiring an analogous ISC register maintained at the registered office and produced to FINTRAC, CRA, securities regulators and law enforcement; Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39. Sanctions statutes: United Nations Act, S.C. 1992, c. 52; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 22; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21. Notarization and authentication: Notaries Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. N.6, and Commissioner for Taking Affidavits Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.17; Hague Apostille Convention in force for Canada as of 11 January 2024 with Global Affairs Canada as the competent authentication authority.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (Ontario OBCA: ISC register remains at the registered office, not publicly filed; mandatory disclosure to FINTRAC, CRA, securities regulators and law enforcement upon lawful demand; Federal CBCA incorporations became Fully_Public under the Canadian public UBO registry effective 22 January 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service and Delivery
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada; if destination state is not a Hague member, full Consular Legalization through Global Affairs Canada and the destination consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Compliance (corporate good standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ontario Business Registry (OBCA entity) or Corporations Canada (federal CBCA entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada; alternatively Consular Legalization for non-Hague destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract from the Individuals with Significant Control (UBO) register, certified by a director or Ontario counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company records and the authorizing Ontario legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada; Consular Legalization where the foreign counterparty requires it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity, address and verification documents of all directors, officers and 25% or greater UBOs (passport, proof of address, banking reference)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ontario notary public or commissioner for taking affidavits
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada; Consular Legalization if the receiving bank is situated in a non-Hague state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number registration and tax account verification statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy with notarization and Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada; Consular Legalization if a foreign authority refuses apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NUANS / Ontario Name Search Report used for the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ontario Business Registry authorized search house or Corporations Canada NUANS service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with apostille, commonly requested by LC issuing banks and correspondent trade finance banks

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance: identify and verify all directors, officers, sole or joint signatories, 25% or greater shareholders and individuals with direct or indirect control in fact; screen each against the Canadian domestic sanctions lists (United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act), UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists (as a contractual requirement of US correspondent banks), and FINTRAC's designated persons lists. For an ISIC 4690 re-invoicing hub rated Medium_Risk_Enhanced, apply enhanced due diligence (EDD) to all beneficial owners, all authorized signatories, high-risk jurisdiction counterparties, and LC/TT/XT payees and payers, including source-of-wealth verification, ongoing transaction monitoring and annual re-screening; domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (heads of state, ministers, senior officials, military leaders, judges, central bank officials, ambassadors, state-owned enterprise executives, political party leaders) and their family members and close associates must be escalated to senior management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry, the official government portal at https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry; NUANS name search accessible through Corporations Canada and authorized Ontario registry service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must consist of a distinctive element and a mandatory legal element in English and/or French, using Limited/Limitee, Incorporated/Incorporee, Corporation/Compagnie or their abbreviations Ltd., Inc., Corp., Ltee. The Ontario registry accepts only Roman-alphabetic characters, numerals and permitted punctuation; non-Roman scripts (including Chinese characters, Cyrillic or Arabic) are not registered as the legal name. A foreign-language or transliterated business style may be used as an unregistered trade name only after the official Ontario name is registered and only if it does not create confusion with existing marks. Federal CBCA names follow the same doctrine under subsection 12(1), requiring a NUANS report and a distinctive element in English or French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected for confusion, conflict or a prohibited token, the applicant shall first obtain an express written consent or authorization from the affected name holder or trademark owner and resubmit the same name with a fresh name search report; alternatively, modify the distinctive element or add a distinguishing initial, numeral or geographic qualifier and refile. If the Director of Corporate Registry still refuses, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request within 30 days to the Director under the Ontario Business Corporations Act, attaching consent letters, a fresh NUANS report and legal submissions distinguishing the marks. A further refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the Ontario Divisional Court (OBCA) or, for federal CBCA incorporations, the Federal Court of Canada. If time is critical, the applicant may incorporate immediately under a numbered name such as 1234567 Ontario Inc. and subsequently apply for a change of name once the preferred name is cleared by court order or consent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Ontario registered office may be a virtual office address only if it is a physical location in Ontario capable of receiving service of process; a post office box or mail-forwarding address alone is prohibited. For a general re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediary (ISIC 4690), a pure virtual office is commercially inadvisable: the opening bank, SWIFT LC issuing bank and correspondent trade finance providers will normally require a real physical office, on-site staff, local books and records, and evidence of decision-making substance. A shell-like virtual address materially increases the risk of bank account refusal, enhanced CRA transfer-pricing scrutiny, loss of treaty benefits and re-characterization of the Canadian entity as a conduit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk assessment: CRA books-and-records review and GST/HST verification for a re-invoicing intermediary of this class is approximately 8-12% over a 36-month operating cycle; FINTRAC direct examination risk is below 5% unless the entity also engages in money services business activity; the bank or LC issuing institution has a 90% or greater practice of conducting a virtual or physical KYC site visit and a 15-25% probability of an unannounced physical visit for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced trade facility. If a pure virtual office is used, the probability of unannounced physical inspection by the bank, CRA or FINTRAC rises to near 100%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, ss. 4-6, 115, 119, 125-128; Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39, s. 2; O. Reg. 62/06 under the B.C.A.; Ontario Business Registry Act, 2021, S.O. 2021, c. 4, Sch. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery - Companies and Corporations Branch (Ontario Business Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 2 - General or Form 3 - with special share provisions) transmitted electronically via the Ontario Business Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow requirement under the OBCA; incorporators may issue shares for par-value consideration or such consideration as the directors fix, and the subscription consideration may be settled as agreed by the board, including intercompany re-invoicing receivables in arm's-length trade transactions
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS Articles of Incorporation were filed in Ontario; NOW BE IT RESOLVED: (1) share subscriptions in the share schedule are accepted, recorded in the share register, and certificates issued; (2) the registered office is established at the Ontario address in the Notice of Registered Office, which the directors shall file within sixty days; (3) By-Law No. 1 is adopted; (4) the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed with customary powers; (5) the officers may open bank accounts with recognized financial institutions; and (6) the officers shall complete all corporate tax and regulatory registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Reservation (NUANS / Ontario Name Search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario - Ontario Business Registry (name search and reservation module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search (or Ontario Name Search on the Registry portal) covering the proposed corporate name for the re-invoicing trade entity; obtain a search report dated no more than 90 days prior to filing; reserve the proposed name for up to 90 days, or elect a numbered company (e.g., 12345678 Ontario Inc.); ensure the name ends with a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., or Incorporate and contains no prohibited or protected terms.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name statement with jurisdiction clause for Ontario
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because of confusion with a prior registration, submit a revised name and new search report, or proceed with a numbered company; there is no administrative appeal for a provincial name refusal; after incorporation, a name change may be effected by filing Articles of Amendment under OBCA s. 168.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and directors (external legal preparation); reviewed by Ontario Business Registry adjudicators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation stating the corporate name, registered office municipal address, share structure (Class A/Class B common/preferred, voting rights, transfer restrictions), business restrictions (e.g., a restriction to domestic and cross-border trade and re-invoicing if desired), and minimum/maximum director count (minimum 1; at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians under OBCA s. 119). Obtain signed consent from each first director; wet signature or digital signature using a qualified signatory.
required_dossiers: Share structure and class rights schedule
Registered office address (municipal 911 address, not a post office box)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adjudicators issue a deficiency notice; correct the offending clauses and re-submit; any correction must be made within 30 days to avoid a new filing deadline; legal counsel re-certifies compliance with OBCA and the Ontario Business Registry form requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Registration Filing, Payment of Fees, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (Companies and Corporations Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Authenticate the signatory on the Ontario Business Registry portal, upload or state the settled Articles, pay the $300 CAD statutory fee (approx. USD 220) by credit card/Interac, and wait for the electronic adjudication; upon approval the registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation (CIF), which establishes legal personality, limited liability, and the corporate birth date for tax and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Name reservation number or NUANS report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the registry returns a reasons-of-rejection notice; cure by amending and refiling within the statutory response period (generally 30 days); if the Certificate is issued with an error, apply for administrative correction or file Articles of Amendment within 6 months for post-issuance corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Adoption of By-Law No. 1, Share Subscription and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal governance); registrable documents to the Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting within 30 days after incorporation; adopt By-Law No. 1 (meetings, directors, officers, execution of documents); pass unanimous board resolutions accepting the share subscriptions in the subscription schedule and recording issuance of share certificates; fix the registered office address; appoint President, Secretary, Treasurer (or CEO/CFO/CSec); within 60 days of incorporation, file Form 1 (Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors) with the Ontario Business Registry and keep a registered office location that is open during normal business hours (address for service).
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing of Form 1 attracts late filings penalty (CAD 70 per form unless the corporation is exempt); the corporation should file immediately with the overdue-filing penalty and, if operational, seek the registrar's forgiveness only for first-time small-late filings; internal governance errors are cured by subsequent board resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration (Income Tax, GST/HST, Payroll)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online (CRA); Ontario Ministry of Finance for Ontario Corporation Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and Form 1 filings, register for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) plus program accounts: corporate income tax (RC0001), GST/HST (RC0002; mandatory once the gross annual revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 - relevant for invoicing/re-invoicing flows), payroll (RC0001 if employees are engaged), and import/export program account (RM - Canadian Border Services Agency) because ISIC 4690 re-invoicing may involve cross-border goods flows; Ontario corporation tax is reported on the CT23 Corporate Tax Return aligned with the federal T2, so confirm the Ontario account linkage at registration.
required_dossiers: Form 1 (Notice of Registered Office and Directors)
Registered office address and directors' identities
Bank account transit numbers (for CRA direct deposit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is delayed, contact CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525) and provide the incorporation file number; for GST/HST registration errors, cancel and re-register program accounts via CRAs My Business Account; if the Ontario CT23 account is not linked, call the Ontario Tax Office to consolidate using the provincial file number shown on the registration notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Premises Assessment and Occupational Safety Positioning (Licensing Absence Confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal business licensing department; regional fire department; WSIB (Workplace Safety and Insurance Board) for employer postings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the activity is pure re-invoicing/wholesale trade intermediation (ISIC 4690 / NAICS 425120), no federal/provincial operating license is triggered; nevertheless, if a physical Ontario office is opened, confirm with the municipality that the location is zoned for commercial office use, obtain a zoning compliance letter or occupancy certificate, and (if staff work on site) complete a fire safety plan per Ontario Fire Code, O. Reg. 213/07 and workplace policy under the Occupational Health and Safety Act; register with WSIB only if employees are employed.
required_dossiers: Lease or occupancy document for the office address
Construction/occupancy certificate (if the building has not been issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality denies an occupancy certificate due to zoning, apply to the Committee of Adjustment for a minor variance, or relocate to a properly zoned commercial office; a fire-safety deficiency is cured by upgrading the fire plan and obtaining a clearance letter from the municipal fire chief; WSIB non-registration is cured retroactively by paying assessed premiums plus penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing board is triggered for wholesale trade agents, brokers and re-invoicing operations (ISIC 4690 / NAICS 425120) under Ontario law; industrial permits apply only to manufacturing, warehousing of dangerous goods, or hazardous waste handling, which are outside the current scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operating or manufacturing permit is required for a general commercial re-invoicing hub; the corporation operates under its Certificate of Incorporation and municipal occupancy rights.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is commercial trade intermediation and re-invoicing with no manufacturing, discharge point, or regulated emission source; no Environmental Assessment (EA) Registration, no Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) and no air/wastewater license is required at formation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at formation; if later adding distribution warehousing, compliance thresholds are those of O. Reg. 419/05 (Air Pollution - Local Air Quality) applying to total suspended particulates/VOC limits, and O. Reg. 199/05 (Municipal and Industrial Sewage) for wastewater; no effluent enters the sanitary sewer from re-invoicing activities; office waste is handled under municipal waste by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: General office tenancy requirements apply: fire safety certification as per Ontario Fire Code O. Reg. 213/07, structural soundness as per Ontario Building Code (Part 3 is applicable only for larger assembly/office buildings), and workplace health & safety certificate for the designated supervisor under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1; a pre-move fire inspection memoranda from the local fire marshal is recommended; no civil-defense shelter designation or industrial site clearance is required for a pure re-invoicing operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); business registration portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); provincial corporate registry: Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services (Ontario Business Registry, https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity deriving Canadian-source business income or making taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA. For a non-resident corporation, file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or the GST/HST Non-Resident Registration package; CRA assigns a BN with program accounts: corporate income tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM/RD). Registration may be completed online via CRA My Business Account or by mailing the completed RC1/RC1A forms to the CRA Sudbury Tax Centre. A non-resident corporation must also appoint a representative (fiscal agent) if it has not established Canadian residency, and such representative must be a Canadian resident or a Canadian corporation authorized to act. The GST/HST account is effective as of the date the entity ceases to be a small supplier or earlier if voluntarily elected. For Ontario HST purposes, the federal BN (with RT program account) is the sole tax identifier; no separate provincial VAT ID exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no IRS-style 'check-the-box' classification regime; corporations are ipso facto entity-level taxpayers under the Income Tax Act (Canada), Part I. Available elections relevant to cross-border re-invoicing: (1) GST/HST joint election under subsection 167(2) of the Excise Tax Act for supplies between closely related corporations (where the recipient is not a financial institution and the supply is not a prescribed supply); (2) Election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act to not use the Quick Method; (3) Annual GST/HST filing election for non-resident registrants under section 239 of the Excise Tax Act; (4) Income Tax Act section 216 election for a non-resident to file a separate return for Canadian rental income and property income; (5) Transfer-pricing contemporaneous documentation election (no formal election but a documentation obligation may be satisfied by electing to use the CRA Form T106 or RC4600 filing method); (6) Hybrid-mismatch rules under sections 18.2 and 18.21 of the Income Tax Act (no elective carve-out is available; the rules apply mandatorily to payments structured to exploit hybrid mismatches).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST—Federal Goods and Services Tax plus Ontario Harmonized Sales Tax (single VAT administered by CRA under the Excise Tax Act; the Ontario provincial portion (8%) is collected as an HST component under the Ontario Retail Sales Tax harmonization effective July 1, 2010). In-bonded re-invoicing transactions may also engage customs duties under the Customs Tariff and the import/re-export regime administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: an entity is a 'small supplier' and exempt from mandatory GST/HST registration unless its worldwide taxable supplies (including associated persons' supplies, excluding capital gains and zero-rated exports) exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the aggregate over the last four consecutive calendar quarters; once the threshold is exceeded, registration is mandatory and becomes effective as of the beginning of the quarter in which the threshold was crossed (Excise Tax Act, subsection 240(1)); exporters and non-residents may voluntarily register below the threshold to claim input tax credits and zero-rate supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance (no continuous transaction control, CTC, API stamping, or digital signature regime analogous to e-invoicing mandates in Italy or France). However: (1) all monthly GST/HST registrants with a filing threshold of CAD 5 million in taxable supplies must file and remit electronically through CRA My Business Account or via EDI/XML protocols (mandatory electronic filing since 2023); (2) the Government of Canada has adopted the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard (PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0, based on the Pan-European Public Procurement On-Line (PEPPOL) network) and, effective 2023, suppliers to federal departments must be able to receive and process e-invoices if the department requests them; (3) taxpayers must retain valid tax invoices (supporting GST/HST registration numbers of supplier and recipient, the amount of tax charged, and the recipient's name) in a retrievable electronic or paper format for six years, but no XML schema validation or government fiscal stamp is imposed; (4) Revenu Québec operates a separate e-invoicing and request-to-pay system under the Pan-Canadian standard for provincial purposes, but this does not apply to Ontario registrants; (5) CRA follows the OECD TIC 3.0 interoperability guidelines for taxpayer data exchange, and GST/HST return information is transmitted using the EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) protocol.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Part VI of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act zero-rates: (a) supplies of tangible personal property exported by the supplier or by a non-resident recipient in accordance with section 1 and 2 of Part V (property delivered to a carrier for export, or export documentation obtained); (b) supplies of services to non-residents under section 7 of Part V where the service is in respect of tangible personal property situated outside Canada, or the service is performed wholly outside Canada, or the service is supplied in respect of real property outside Canada, or (for advisory/similar services) the recipient is a non-resident and the services are not for consumption in Canada; (c) arranging for or assisting in the export of goods by a registrant (section 8 of Part V), which covers a re-invoicing intermediary or trade agent whose supply consists of arranging the export of Canadian goods; (d) commercial re-invoicing hubs may claim zero-rating where title to the goods passes outside Canada (delivery terms DAP/FOB foreign port) and the supplier maintains contemporaneous records proving disposal outside Canada. For supplies of goods that are not shipped from Canada (pure offshore re-invoicing, STO/string sales), the place-of-supply rules in rules 1-3 apply: if the goods are not delivered in Canada and are not exported from Canada, the supply is generally outside the scope of GST/HST if the supplier is a non-resident, but for a Canadian supplier it may be deemed to be made in Canada or outside Canada depending on whether the goods are situated in Canada at the time of supply; such offshore intercompany transfers should be documented as offshore services or agency disbursements rather than Canadian taxable supplies to eliminate unintended domestic VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: G13/CBSA Customs Export Declaration (Canadian Export Reporting via CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CAERS) or ACE Canada Export Reporting, including AESDirect equivalent; for low-value shipments, the commercial invoice may substitute only where no B13A is required)
Bill of Lading (through or master B/L evidencing shipment from Canada to a foreign destination or delivery at a foreign port)

Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Inward Remittance Advice (bank SWIFT MT103/MT202 or bank statement evidencing settlement of export proceeds from the non-resident buyer to the Canadian exporter within the mandated repatriation window)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange policy and regulatory oversight are administered by the Department of Finance Canada, with AML/trade-screening supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a freely floating exchange rate regime with no exchange controls and full convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current and capital account items. Dividends, interest, management fees, trade settlements, and profit remittances may be transferred cross-border without foreign-exchange regulatory approval. The only material hurdles are tax compliance (e.g., Part XIII withholding tax, transfer-pricing documentation), PCMLTFA reporting thresholds, and bank-level client due diligence. No Canadian central bank authorization is required for currency conversion or remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender rules and no mandatory conversion ratio. A Canadian re-invoicing exporter is not legally required to repatriate or convert foreign-currency export proceeds. However, all revenues and foreign-currency transactions must be reported in Canadian dollars for Income Tax Act purposes using the relevant Bank of Canada or book exchange rate, and cash or negotiable instrument transactions of CAD 10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Operational Account (CAD and USD multi-currency treasury platform)
Commercial Operating Account with Global Trade Finance Suite
International Settlement Account and LC-Issuance Account
Re-Invoicing Hub Account with dedicated FX Desk
Commercial Operating Account plus Letter of Credit E-Trade Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury or escrow provider. Offshore digital EMIs and non-bank fintech institutions are not chartered banks under Canada's Bank Act and cannot lawfully accept deposits or provide full clearing/escrow services from within Canada. They may be used as ancillary payment-service providers for FX execution or remittance support, but the core capital escrow, commercial LC, and SWIFT settlement infrastructure must sit with a Schedule I bank or an authorized foreign bank branch duly registered in Canada.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for all directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signing officers at initial account opening for a newly incorporated re-invoicing entity. Most Schedule I banks accept a video-verified KYC interview only where there is a pre-existing banking relationship or introduction by a regulated Canadian legal counsel or accountant. In practice, first-time corporate entities are required to appear in-branch or complete a notarized remote interview with a Canadian-based professional. FINTRAC rules permit regulated non-face-to-face verification if prescribed measures are used, but bank risk policies for medium-risk re-invoicing traders typically mandate physical or video-verified appearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction payables/receivables connected to non-OECD wholesale re-invoicing corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership pack, board resolution describing the commercial re-invoicing model, corporate organizational chart, complete customer and supplier due diligence files, audited financial statements or management accounts, underlying purchase and resale contracts, invoices and bills of lading, sanctions and UBO screening results, and source-of-wealth declarations for non-resident shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow funding from an offshore parent or third-party affiliate with no clear economic rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notice, notarized subscription and share allotment agreement, lender-bank confirmation letter, prior intercompany transaction ledger, OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation (including comparable analysis), and SWIFT wire narratives stating 'direct investment' or 'paid-in capital' supported by a directors' resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid 'pass-through' settlement pattern consistent with layering, structuring, or unexplained round-tripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade control narrative and operating flowchart, inventory and receivable aging reports, complete SWIFT MT103 archive, transport documents (bill of lading, customs declarations), supplier invoices with matching LC terms, front-to-back commercial contracts, and intercompany dual-offset reconciliation statements certified by a Canadian CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent high-value FX conversions without an articulated hedging or treasury rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy, hedge and FX risk assessment, hedged transaction worksheets, executed FX tickets and dealer confirmations, delegation of signing authority, treasury committee minutes, and independent valuation models demonstrating currency exposure arising from invoicing baskets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital is routed as a SWIFT MT103 business credit transfer to the Canadian bank through a correspondent clearing relationship. Canada does not mandate a central-bank authorization or purpose-code registry; however, for FINTRAC client identification and the bank's internal Accountable-Transaction monitoring, the remittance information line must clearly state 'capital subscription' or 'paid-in capital / foreign direct investment.' The first injection should be accompanied by a certified board resolution, share subscription ledger, source-of-funds statements, and a bank-signed escrow direction where the account is a dedicated capital escrow account. Deposits denominated in foreign currency will be converted at the bank's posted arm's-length rate, and the resulting Canadian-dollar balance will be recorded for Income Tax Act reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to third-party suppliers are cleared through the following compliant rails: SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for direct wire payments to overseas beneficiary accounts; SWIFT MT700 (documentary letter of credit) for import/export purchase transactions requiring payment against presentation of shipping documents; SWIFT MT760 (standby letter of credit) as a performance or payment guarantee; and bank-to-bank correspondent transfers through Fedwire or CHIPS for USD clearances involving U.S. counterparties. For re-invoicing operations, every payment must be matched to the underlying supply invoice, transport document, and customs declaration in order to preserve trade-payment characterization and avoid risking rejection or enhanced review as a remittance of unknown origin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and other freely convertible pairs executed under an ISDA/CSA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on underlying receivables or payables denominated in controlled or non-convertible currencies, subject to bank risk-policy approval and commercial justification
Cross-currency swaps for long-term trade receivables and intra-group financing with matched cash flows
Listed FX futures or vanilla OTC FX options entered on regulated Canadian exchanges or with authorized dealer banks for hedging purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Business Corporations Act Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, ServiceOntario (Ontario Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation, continuation, or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 10 per month or partial month, capped at CAD 100; failure to file for a sustained period of one year or more permits administrative dissolution under OBCA s. 240.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Ontario corporate tax allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Corporate Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30 of following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat failure penalty 10%; CRA may arrange for tax returns to be filed under threat of prosecution; no direct corporate registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold triggers a mandatory audit for a non-public Ontario Business Corporation. An audit is required only when articles or by-laws mandate it, a shareholder unanimous waiver under OBCA s. 149 is not passed, the corporation is a reporting issuer/TSX-listed, or a sector regulator (e.g., financial or insurance services) imposes statutory annual audit obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook - IFRS as issued by the IASB, or Part II - Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); ASPE is the standard framework for typical unlisted re-invoicing trade corporations absent external lender or shareholder requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: OBCA s. 140.2 requires an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register to be maintained at the registered office and updated within 15 calendar days upon any knowledge of changes in significant control or share transfers. Ontario does not require an annual UBO confirmation filing to the registry; nevertheless, an annual internal recertification of beneficial ownership, share transfer reconciliation, and director/minute book review is performed as the corporate secretarial governance standard.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 - 510 per year (typical Ontario registered agent and corporate secretarial services for a private business corporation)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 12,000 per year (typical certified audit and statement preparation for a mid-sized re-invoicing trade corporation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory headline rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax + 11.5% Ontario general corporate income tax. Non-resident-owned or captive re-invoicing entities do not qualify for CCPC preferential rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or investment tax incentives exist for ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing operations in Ontario. Ontario denies the small business deduction (Ontario 3.2% federal 9% combined 12.2%) for a CCPC to the extent income is 'specified corporate income' derived from associated non-resident re-invoicing or services (ITA s. 256(1.1)); federal SR&ED credits and Ontario innovation tax credits require genuine R&D and are irrelevant to a trade intermediary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (RC101) filed via CRA EFILE/TEI (T2 E-File); mandatory electronic filing if gross revenue exceeds CAD 1,000,000, otherwise paper T2 is acceptable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; instalments of tax payable generally due on a monthly basis for large corporations, or in equal installments based on the prior year's tax liability if first-time filer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nine-digit Canada Revenue Agency business number; a non-resident corporation must obtain a BN and refer to the CRA corporation account (RC account) on all remittances and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident re-invoicing company carrying on business in Canada quotes its BN and, if no BN issued, applies under the CRA non-resident registration procedure before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Month, day and year of the corporation's taxation year-end; the first fiscal period cannot exceed 53 weeks without CRA approval.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation's Canadian branch fiscal period should coincide with the head-office fiscal year unless CRA permits otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification as 'Resident in Canada' or 'Non-resident of Canada'; residence is determined by incorporation in Canada, central management and control, or deeming rules under ITA s. 250.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation files T2 only if it 'carries on business in Canada'; income is limited to Canadian-source business income attributable to a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 - Federal Tax Calculation (Line 380 Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after all Part I adjustments, cross-border arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments, and loss carryovers; federal tax at 15% before abatement and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident multi-jurisdictional re-invoicing hub must allocate taxable income between Canadian and foreign permanent establishments on a formulary basis consistent with the arm's-length principle and is bound by CRA transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 2 - Ontario Provincial Tax (Line 860 Ontario Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile Ontario taxable income and apply the 11.5% Ontario general rate; non-resident corporations compute Ontario tax only on income allocable to an Ontario permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Ontario permanent establishment exists, the Ontario allocation is nil; a re-invoicing hub with an Ontario office, employees, contracts, invoices and bank accounts generally has an Ontario permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 9 - Non-Capital and Net Capital Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim non-capital losses carryforward up to 20 years and carryback 3 years; net capital losses carryback 3 years and forward indefinitely.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may deduct only non-capital losses that are reasonably attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment; losses realized outside Canada cannot shelter Canadian-source re-invoicing profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim federal and Ontario foreign tax credits for foreign-source income tax paid by the Canadian corporation, limited to the Canadian tax otherwise payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation normally does not claim foreign tax credits on T2 except when Canadian tax is imposed on foreign-source income and treaty relief is not otherwise available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months); failure to use electronic filing where mandated: CAD 250 fixed penalty; interest is charged at the CRA prescribed rate on unpaid installments and balances. Willful failure to file can trigger gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents, filed through CRA My Business Account or certified EFILE software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (aligned with the T2 due date).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I - Identification of Canadian Taxpayer
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, BN, fiscal year-end, and description of the business of the Canadian filer and each controlled foreign affiliate or non-resident counterparty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian-resident re-invoicing hub must file T106 for each non-resident non-arm's-length person when the aggregate value of transactions with that person exceeds CAD 1,000,000; the form captures purchases, sales, commissions, fees, interest, royalties, management fees and intercompany balances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II - Transaction Details and Pricing Method
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each transaction category, amounts, contractual terms, and the transfer pricing method applied (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For off-shore re-invoicing, the gross invoice amount to third-party customers and the related intercompany buy/sell price must be separately disclosed; the margin retained in Canada must be defensible under the arm's-length standard.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106 or false information: CAD 100 per day, minimum CAD 1,000 and maximum CAD 25,000 per failure, in addition to transfer pricing penalties and interest; failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation forfeits 'reasonable efforts' defense against the 10% TP penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NR4 - Non-Resident Tax Withholding, Remitting and Reporting Return (NR4 Summary and NR4 slips), submitted via CRA My Business Account or approved payroll software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: NR4 slips and summary must be filed by March 31 of the calendar year following the year in which the non-resident was paid or credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Recipient Identification (Name, Address, Country of Residence)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the beneficial owner of the payment including a certificate of residence for treaty-reduced rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Canadian re-invoicing entity pays dividends, royalties, interest or management fees to a non-resident, it must remit Part XIII withholding tax at 25% unless a treaty reduction is substantiated before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Income Code and Gross Amount Paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify each payment: dividends (code 29), interest (code 30), royalties (code 28), rents, or management fees; withheld tax is shown at 25% or treaty rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A re-invoicing hub must not net intercompany settlements without considering withholding on deemed or constructive payments; valuations and price adjustments triggering additional cross-border payments must be separately reported.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete NR4 filing: CAD 25 per day per slip with escalating penalties; unreported Part XIII withholding can be reassessed at 25% of gross payments, plus interest, 50% gross-negligence penalties, and director liability for the unremitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax under ITA s. 212(2) on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to non-residents; a Canadian re-invoicing hub is the withholding agent and must remit on gross dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit: (i) a completed CRA Form NR301 (or treaty-specific form) declaring eligibility for treaty benefits; (ii) a current Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty-resident tax authority; and (iii) documentary evidence of beneficial ownership and, where required under the treaty, minimum ownership thresholds (e.g., 10% voting shares for the 5% Canada-US dividend rate). The payer must withhold at the domestic 25% rate until complete documentation is in hand; refunds of over-withheld Part XIII tax are claimed by the non-resident on Form NR7-R within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII WHT is 25% on both royalties (ITA s. 212(1)(d)) and certain interest (ITA s. 212(1)(b); arm's-length interest paid to unrelated persons may be exempt under domestic law). Treaty rates are generally 0%-15% depending on the DTA and payment type: e.g., Canada-US treaty commonly reduces arm's-length interest to 0% or 15% in limited cases and royalties to 0% for copyright, patents, trademarks and similar intangibles; non-treaty payments remain at 25%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory revenue threshold requires a Local File or Master File in Canada; however, contemporaneous TP documentation is required as a condition of the 'reasonable efforts' defense. Mandatory filing thresholds: (i) T106 Information Return if non-arm's-length transactions with any non-resident exceed CAD 1,000,000; (ii) Country-by-Country Report (CBCR) where the multinational group consolidates revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000; (iii) TP penalty applies when the gross adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations like offshore financial centres; nevertheless, an economic substance doctrine is enforced through: (i) General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, ITA s. 245) denying tax benefits from transactions lacking genuine business purpose; (ii) Transfer pricing recharacterization under ITA s. 247; (iii) treaty shopping defences under DTA LOB/PPT articles; (iv) the principle of corporate residence requiring central management and control in Canada with real employees, premises, contracts and risk management; and (v) CRS/FATCA reporting exposing low-substance shell arrangements. An Ontario re-invoicing hub must demonstrate real decision-making, risk-bearing, and intercompany contracts to avoid CRA reattribution of profit to a foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Part XIII Withholding Tax (Profit Repatriation Failure)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest or management fees to a non-resident shareholder or affiliate without withholding and remitting 25% (or treaty rate) to the Receiver General of Canada; netting intercompany invoices without Part XIII remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment for the full gross amount of unwithheld tax plus CRA prescribed interest; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the unremitted amount (ITA s. 163(2)); failure to deduct/withhold under ITA s. 227(8) creates a separate liability equal to the amount not withheld.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unremitted Part XIII tax under ITA s. 227.1, including interest and penalties; CRA can collect from personal assets, register liens, and pursue civil recovery; egregious failure may lead to an injunction prohibiting the director from leaving Canada and surrender of passports.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misdeclaration and T106 Non-Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking excessive profit margins in Canada without economic substance, manipulating intercompany purchase prices, failing to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation, or failing to file T106 for transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing recharacterization adjusting arm's-length price; a penalty equal to 10% of the gross transfer pricing adjustment when the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue, unless the taxpayer demonstrates 'reasonable efforts'; separate T106 penalties up to CAD 25,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false TP documentation or participate in a scheme to shift profits to a tax haven may be assessed as promoters or counsel under ITA s. 239 (counselling tax evasion), exposing them to fines of 50%-200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil liability can arise for breach of fiduciary duty to creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GAAR - Artificial Shell / Low Substance Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating an Ontario corporation solely to access treaty benefits or avoid foreign tax, without employees, offices, bank accounts, contracts, commercial risk, or business activity; circular re-invoicing flows designed to obtain a tax benefit and constituting 'avoidance transactions'.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax benefit is annulled and the transaction recharacterized; GAAR penalty of 25% of the benefit under ITA s. 245(8); redetermination of foreign tax credits and potential reallocation of income to the true economic owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell re-invoicing corporation can be personally assessed for the recovered tax if the corporation is insolvent or when a 'stop order' under the Income Tax Act is used to collect unpaid corporate tax from directors; criminal liability arises where misleading statements or books were created to conceal the arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Evasion and Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of revenue, false invoicing, fabricated intercompany contracts (dummy invoices), concealment of beneficial owners, or using the trade payments rail to obscure the origin of funds; failing to implement an AML program when acting as an electronic money transfer intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under ITA s. 239: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment of up to 5 years; under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) penalties for unregistered MSB activity and missing FATCA/FINTRAC reporting reach CAD 500,000 on summary conviction and CAD 1,000,000 on indictment; customs and trade misinvoicing penalties apply under the Customs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The 'piercing the corporate veil' doctrine applies in cases of fraud and sham transactions; director personal liability covers restitution, legal costs, fines, and civil damages; courts may issue travel bans, surrender of passports, freeze personal bank accounts, and impose imprisonment; directorial resignation does not extinguish liability if the director was complicit in the evasion.
